title: Regulation of Compensation and Systemic Risk: Evidence from the UK

scopes.description: All supplied 01_data_build.do preparation, UK/EU/US systemic-risk, VLab, compensation, matching and final variable-construction stages. The appendix regression tables are contextual; no paper-wide regression driver is supplied in this package.

requirements.description: The combined `ciq_banksope` input used to supplement EU/US bank compensation/accounting. The code expects the combined author-prepared table with CTYPE* and DATA* fields; which fields came from Compustat Capital IQ versus Bankscope, and the actual source keys/types, are unresolved. Catalog candidates are discovery evidence only.

The separate UK_FX yearly currency conversion input consumed by the EU/US bank compensation conversion branch. Its producer, source, date convention and expected exchange-rate units are not supplied or established in the package.

The Markit CDS input (`wrds_markit.dta`) and the author's matching identifiers/series needed by the bank and UK CDS branches. Required series, historical vintage, identifiers, row coverage and relationship to the downstream Markit subset files remain unresolved; treat those regional transformations separately from the source input.

requirements.description: The distinct UK hand-collected FactSet_ownership UK file used by the ownership branch, plus its company identifiers, dates, ownership and option-holding fields. The author-prepared file and its field/key contract are not packaged or verified.

The distinct EU FactSet_ownership file read by the supplied script, with the author-collected ownership records and the exact identifiers/period expected by its merge. No compatible file is packaged; regional coverage and schema remain unknown.

The separate US FactSet_ownership input referenced by the ownership branch, including the author-collected records and matching key/period. The file is absent from this package and its schema/coverage are unverified.

The hand-collected bank CEO forced/unforced turnover and destination-history input (`bank_ceo_turnover`) consumed in the supplied build. Its exact firm/person identifiers, date coding, regional sample and observation history are not supplied.

UK daily macro state input `CoVAR_M_inputs.dta`, separately consumed by the UK systemic-risk branch. The code expects UK series including `d3M_Yield_UKTR`, `A10YRTR_3MTR`, `A3MLIBOR_3MTR`, and `Moodys_BAA_TR10YR` alongside the UK market series; source naming, units, dates, joins and full construction history are unverified. The code comment states the downloaded sample starts in 2001 for CoVaR lags, before its 2006–2012 analysis window.

EU daily macro state input `CoVAR_M_inputs_EU.dta`, separate from both UK and US contracts. Code expects `d3M_Yield_EUTR`, `A10YREUTR_3MEUTR`, `A3MEURIBOR_3MEUTR`, and `Moodys_BAA_EUTR10YR` alongside EU market series. The datasheet names FactSet and Datastream inputs, but exact dates, units, fields, identifiers and the 2001-plus lag history remain unverified.

US daily macro state input `CoVAR_M_inputs_US.dta`, distinct from the UK and EU files. Code expects `d3M_Yield_USTR`, `A10YRUSTR_3MUSTR`, `A3MLIBOR_3MUSTR`, `Moodys_BAA_USTR10YR`, and US market fields including `sprtrn`; the datasheet names CRSP, FRED and FactSet. Exact author construction, units, field schema and lag history remain unverified.

The exact EU membership workbook imported by the VLab country-filter stage (`eu_member_states 2018-01-12.xlsx`, sheet `data`, range A1:B29 with first row as headers). It is not included in the package; the country-code and membership labels must match the lookup merge.

Per-firm SRISK/LRMES VLab CSV series for the relevant country population, used to generate `SRISK_VLAB` and later full-country denominator aggregates. The code initializes normalized columns such as date, lrmes, varday, beta, corr_msci, lvg_ratio, srisk and mkt_cap, but the raw CSV schema, 2018 vintage, country/firm population and historical field compatibility are unresolved. Do not restrict this input to study-firm identifiers because the code aggregates across the loaded country population.

issues.kind: unverified author input availability and compatibility
issues.description: The package inventory contains the 01_data_build.do source, datasheet, appendix and all_identifiers_final.xlsx, but none of the consumed study panels or raw/prepared tables. The workbook is an identifier list, not a firm-year analysis panel. The named data requirements are retained individually; current local or commercial availability, source fields, keys, units and periods remain unknown rather than blocked.

The supplied do-file consumes several separately named prepared tables for which it provides no matching producer, including Master_Market_all_UK, BS_RI_Market_new, BS_Master_Market_RI_update_ck, US_Market_return, BS_Master_Market_RI, BS_Master_Market_MV_update_ck, Markit and IDS identifier updates, indg_crosswalk, UK_BIRPU_indicators, EU_US_Bank_indicators, EU_flags, UK_compensation_master, changes_all, and bonus_changes. It also reads all_IDs; the packaged identifier workbook is a plausible crosswalk candidate, but its staging and coverage are unverified. The source supplies some indicator definitions and flags, so this gap concerns file projection/staging, keys and producer-consumer schemas rather than unknown indicator definitions.

The UK Idio_Risk and EU/US BS_Idio_Risk tables are consumed as prepared inputs, but the supplied program does not define their producer, risk/volatility recipe, fields or sample history. Their contract cannot be replaced by the price/return series without changing the authored risk construction.

issues.kind: VLab lookup, population and directory handoff
issues.description: The code imports/filter lookup.dat with the EU membership workbook and produces lookup.dta under $modified\Analysis, then reads the generated basename from $data\SRISK_VLab. The matching output exists in the supplied source; changing the consumer to the known producer path is a supported staging edit. The full-population and current-versus-2018 VLab series questions remain separate.

The code saves markit_bank_subset and markit_uk_subset in the current directory and then reads each under $modified. Aligning the two supplied producers to the existing modified-directory consumers is a supported path edit. The separately consumed markit_identifiers table still has no producer and is tracked in I_PREP_PRODUCERS.

The UK, EU and US macro-state contracts remain separate. The EU branch produces EU_CoVAR_M_inputs_daily under $modified while its consumer uses the same basename under $data; the US branch produces S_CoVAR_M_inputs_daily and later reads a US_CoVAR_M_inputs_daily alias. Aligning these known generated files' paths/names is a supported configuration edit; it does not settle the distinct macro inputs, field mapping or CoVaR sample definitions.

The script initializes `$path` as a relative ..\Regulation_of_Compensation value and then changes the current directory to `$path\00_Original_Data` before defining the downstream globals. Because that relative macro is re-expanded after the directory change, the project root must be anchored before the first `cd` in a working copy.

Three supplied path calls use $modifed while setup defines $modified: the IDS static merge, Markit bank-spread merge, and change to Analysis. Correcting the misspelling is a supported path-configuration edit; it does not produce the missing prepared tables.

The matching stage ends with a bare quoted Master_Accounting_Market_covar_contracts_match target and replace option after the matching results. Adding the ordinary Stata save token preserves the supplied dataset name and matching design.
The supplied US build has one redundant closing quote after the unchanged `temp_2` filename. Removing that extra quote preserves the specified temporary output path.

The VLab series directory loop concatenates every .dta file in the current outputdata folder, and the later country-year denominator sums SRISK over the loaded firms. The full eligible country/firms population, historical vintage, CSV field/schema compatibility and prevention of stale-file inclusion must be established; study identifiers alone do not provide this denominator.

issues.kind: imported and derived BS_Return name collision
issues.description: The bank-market input loop includes BS_Return and renames its imported M variable to that name; the later source line generates BS_Return from BS_RI under the same variable name. The source supports a possible gen-to-replace syntax repair only if the computed ratio is meant to overwrite the imported series. actions.description: Locate compatible author-prepared inputs and reconcile every named table contract before any run. Treat catalogued and historical vendor products as candidate routes, not evidence of current access or compatible fields.
steps: For every requirement, locate the exact author-prepared table or documented source extract and record its product/version, native columns, row unit, identifier keys, date fields, units, frequency and full coverage; use the named table contracts rather than combining unrelated products.

Keep the UK IDS Static, Remuneration, Grants, LTIP and IDS_Companies inputs separate from UK Datastream MV/P/RI/Return/PTBV/DPS/RI_Market and the annual Sales/accounting tables. Credit Datastream as the documented primary UK source; retain Compustat Global only as a documented supplemental candidate unless a specific table mapping is established.

Keep each EU/US BS_* input separate and distinct from the single combined ciq_banksope author table. Confirm the Capital IQ and BankScope field mapping for that combined table rather than treating the brands as interchangeable or as separate mandatory inputs.

Retain region-specific ownership, turnover, FX, crosswalk and compensation-change inputs. For every named prepared table with no in-source producer, locate the earlier author stage or exact file/schema; do not invent a source, risk formula, sample rule or join.

Confirm input history relative to each constructed measure. The code comment requires source history from 2001 for CoVaR lag construction even though the main analysis period is 2006–2012. Verify commercial access from an actual permitted route; a catalog miss is not an access denial.

review_notes: Read the complete cached 2,793-line Stata source, the full datasheet and the full online appendix. The assessed scope is the single supplied 01_data_build.do workflow, including its UK, EU, US, VLab, Markit, compensation and matching branches. The appendix's regression tables are publication context; no separate paper-wide regression/table driver is included in this package.

The only workbook is all_identifiers_final.xlsx. Its bounded probe reads one row and reports CIQ_companyid, DS_Type, isin and sedol; it is a candidate crosswalk for all_IDs, with source/import mapping and coverage unresolved, and it is not a firm-year analysis panel. No analysis_only scope is supported.

The source comments identify a 2006–2012 main period and a 2001-start downloaded sample for CoVaR lags. UK, EU and US market/state-input contracts remain separate. VLab country-year denominators use all loaded positive-SRISK firms, so the full relevant country/firm population and the prevention of stale .dta inputs remain unresolved.

The datasheet names IDS, Datastream, Compustat Capital IQ/Global, Bankscope, Markit, FactSet/financial statements, CRSP/FRED and VLab sources. Commercial entitlement and compatible exports were not established by catalog metadata. The datasheet's IDS proprietary statement conflicts with its later no-proprietary-data statement; no access barrier was inferred. Current official VLab download guidance is a public candidate but is not verified against the authors' January 2018 per-firm files.

Only bounded Stata 18 `which` checks for commands invoked by this source were performed. mdesc, covar, psmatch2 and outreg2 were not found; _crcslbl was found. No author code, risk model, matching routine or regression was run, and no software or data were installed or acquired.

Preservation limitation: the copied feasibility helper source was saved before its failed help invocation and the failure is retained. Initial resource/catalog helper calls imported packages.py/resources.py before both imported helper bytes had been copied into probes; the snapshots saved later are not represented as the original first-execution bytes, and the missing prior bytes were not reconstructed. The captured failed-helper and bare-python subcommand attempts are retained with commands, return codes and separate streams.

A narrow correction pass now proposes a stable `c(pwd)`-anchored project root before the initial `cd`, adds the supplied matching output's ordinary save token, and removes the redundant quote in the existing temp_2 target. These are preparation edits only; no source was modified or run.

The EU/US bank branch imports BS_Return in its market loop and later attempts to generate BS_Return from BS_RI under the same name. The input-versus-derived return definition is retained as unresolved; gen-to-replace is mentioned only as a conditional syntax remedy if that is the authored intent.
